evals.name: coupon-double-redeem-race
evals.prompt: Users can redeem the same single-use coupon twice if they click fast. src/services/coupons.ts loads the coupon, checks `coupon.usedAt == null`, then saves it with usedAt = now(). Postgres + Prisma. Fix it so it can never happen.
evals.expected_output: Replaces check-then-act with an atomic conditional update (updateMany/UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL, checking the affected row count) or a unique constraint on redemptions, maps the conflict to a clear domain error, and adds a concurrency test that fires parallel redemptions and asserts exactly one succeeds.
expectations: The fix is enforced by the database (conditional update with row-count check, unique constraint, or row lock), not by an in-memory check
A second concurrent redemption results in a defined error rather than a silent success
Adds a test that runs redemptions concurrently and asserts exactly one succeeds
Does not rely on a mocked database for the concurrency test

evals.name: not-null-column-on-large-table
evals.prompt: We need a NOT NULL `status` column on `orders` (PostgreSQL, about 40 million rows, migrations with Flyway) defaulting to 'pending'. The app runs 4 replicas with rolling deploys. Write the migration(s).
evals.expected_output: An expand/contract plan: add the column in a way that avoids a table rewrite or long lock, backfill in batches if needed, enforce NOT NULL via a NOT VALID check constraint then VALIDATE (or explain that a constant default makes it metadata-only on PG11+), set lock_timeout, and state which steps are separate deploys.
expectations: Avoids a single blocking ALTER that rewrites or scans 40M rows under an exclusive lock, or explains why the chosen statement is metadata-only
Sets a lock_timeout (or equivalent) for the migration
Explains compatibility with old and new code during the rolling deploy
Does not edit an already-applied migration

evals.name: email-sent-for-rolled-back-order
evals.prompt: Customers sometimes get an order-confirmation email for orders that don't exist. OrderService.placeOrder opens a transaction, inserts the order, calls emailClient.sendConfirmation(), then inserts the order lines — and the lines insert fails sometimes on a constraint.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the side effect inside the transaction as the cause, moves the email out via a transactional outbox or an after-commit hook with an idempotent sender, and adds a test proving no email is sent when the transaction rolls back.
expectations: Names the email call inside the transaction as the root cause
Sends the email only after commit (outbox table or after-commit hook), never inside the transaction
Makes the email sending idempotent or mentions duplicate-delivery handling
Adds a test asserting no email is sent when the order fails to persist
